headline: The US Food and Drug Administration has listed finishing its guidance on AI-enabled medical devices and surgical robots among its priorities for the 2027 fiscal year.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: the headline matches the article, though the list is a proposal and not yet an action.
importance_line: Medical device makers and AI developers learn which FDA advice the agency is putting first for the coming year, and patients would see any effect only later, but it is a list of plans open to comment until 30 Nov, and some of last year's goals are still unfinished.
summary: MedTech Dive reports that the FDA has proposed its priority list of guidance documents (written advice to device makers) for fiscal 2027, including finishing its advice on AI-enabled devices and on robot-assisted surgery, and starting a draft on AI chatbot-style devices for mental health conditions. The lists are proposals and the FDA is taking feedback until 30 Nov.
notes: Single trade outlet; the FDA's own list was not read. The article gives no date for the FDA's list, so freshness is taken from the 2 Oct 2026 publication.
